summary: Ends the FYI (For Your Information) sub-series of RFCs, which RFC 1150 created for the IETF User Services Area, a body that no longer exists. The IESG does not plan to add more FYI documents. It also obsoletes RFC 1150 and moves it to Historic.

plainLanguage.summary: FYI was a special shelf in the library for helpful guides. Since the group that stocked it is gone, this note says no more books will be added to the shelf.

subtitle: The IESG formally closes the FYI series of informational RFCs and retires the rules that created it.

tldr.problem: The FYI sub-series of RFCs was set up for an IETF User Services Area that has not met since March 2001, so the procedures behind it no longer applied.
tldr.mechanism: The IESG records that it will make no further additions to the FYI sub-series, keeps the existing FYI numbers as reference points, and moves RFC 1150 to Historic.
tldr.outcome: No new RFC gets an FYI number. The 38 FYI numbers already assigned stay valid for citation.

today: RFC 6360 obsoletes RFC 1150 and moves it to Historic. It has not been obsoleted itself, and the FYI sub-series stays closed to new additions.

sections.title: Background on the FYI Series
sections.content:
The For Your Information (FYI) sub-series was established by RFC 1150 in 1990 for the IETF User Services Area. It was meant to give Internet users a repository of information about the Internet that might interest a wide range of people.

The User Services Area has not met since IETF 53 in March 2001. Since 1990 a total of 38 FYI numbers have been assigned, and many other Informational RFCs were published that were never part of the sub-series.
sections.plainLanguage: FYI was a shelf of helpful guides run by a club. The club stopped meeting a long time ago, and the shelf only ever held a few dozen books.

sections.title: Ending the Sub-Series
sections.content:
The IESG does not intend to make any further additions to the FYI sub-series. It will keep producing Informational RFCs, but none of them will be given an FYI number.

RFCs that are already in the sub-series keep their FYI numbers, and those numbers can still be used in citations. If a future RFC obsoletes an existing FYI document, the new RFC will not get an FYI number.
sections.plainLanguage: No new books get a shelf label, but the books already labelled keep their labels.

sections.title: RFC 1150 Moved to Historic
sections.content:
This document moves RFC 1150 to Historic and obsoletes it. The procedural information in RFC 1150 is no longer valid.

If it ever becomes desirable to add to the FYI sub-series again, new procedures can be developed to replace this document. The RFC says no Internet security issues are anticipated by these actions.
sections.plainLanguage: The old rulebook for the shelf is put away as history. If someone wants the shelf back, they would write new rules.

references.text: Malkin, G. and J. Reynolds, "FYI on FYI: Introduction to the FYI Notes", FYI 1, RFC 1150, March 1990.
